entities.summary: Cyrus Pallonji Mistry was an Irish businessman. He was the chairman of the Tata Group, an Indian business conglomerate, from 2012 to 2016. He was the sixth chairman of the group, and only the second not to bear the surname Tata. In mid-2012, he was chosen by a selection panel to head the Tata Group and took charge in December that year. In October 2016, the board of Tata Group's holding company, Tata Sons, voted to remove Mistry from the post of chairman. Former chairman Ratan Tata then returned as interim chairman, and Natarajan Chandrasekaran was named as the new chairman a few months later.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Cyrus Pallonji Mistry's tenure as chairman of the Tata Group had significant regional impact in South Asia, particularly in India, where his leadership influenced the conglomerate's strategic direction. His removal from office led to a change in leadership and succession plans within the group.
